scope: Bounded reusable grid topology/interpolation cache, eight dimension pairs, under 2 MiB typed arrays. Heights, errors, targets and coarse indices remain per-call independent. Authoritative hole topology unchanged. Global cache survives scene disposal outside per-world counters.

cpuComparison.note: CPU-only 32x32 terrain LOD preparation, varying heights, unchanged topology and exact indices/targets/error hash in all modes. First call is reported separately; current second trial reuses the cache. Timings exclude hashes/input preparation and are not FPS.

worldBefore.note: Pre-cache 1080p RTX traversal, completed 08:03:04 local, before Modern Standby began. Power state not captured. No controlled FPS speedup is inferred.

worldAfter.note: Three laps, 1080p RTX 5060 Laptop GPU. Windows reported battery power at 27% before awake tests and 23% during the final traversal. No concurrent builds/tests/benchmarks/encoders. No load/render errors; tracked cleanup counters zero. Steady 30 FPS still fails.

validation.cacheTests: Five legacy byte-exact signatures; independent shifted heights, returned-buffer mutation, cache eviction, authoritative holes. All aggregate benchmark output hashes match across 2000 builds.
validation.browser: Windows Chrome 155 native WebGPU on RTX 5060; world, native PBR/resize and density/upload probe pass after cache change. Earlier native motion, shadow/crossfade, two-renderer sharing and authoring recovery scenarios passed during the foliage pass (12 distinct scenarios across this work).

interruptedRun.reason: Confirmed Windows Modern Standby. System log Kernel-Power 506 at 08:03:20 local (idle timeout), 507 at 08:52:14 (keyboard wake). The world browser check stalled with a GPU queue timeout and passed in a fresh browser in 26.5 seconds after wake. The earlier pre-awake microbenchmark is excluded; CPU comparison in this file was rerun after wake. Exploratory CPU sampling was used to identify the triangle-search function, not as quantitative timing evidence.

limits: CPU preparation speedup is not an equal FPS multiplier. Main-thread tile/geometry preparation and shader/upload scheduling remain expensive.
Single world trials with different/unknown power conditions do not establish a controlled before/after FPS gain.
No full browser suite, other GPUs, Linux/software or dense banana/jacaranda render benchmark.
Bounded global topology tables remain resident after scene disposal and are not included in per-world counters.
